hook.situation: You tried a new restaurant, class, cafe, or event and want to tell a friend what you noticed. The point is not just that something happened, but that you personally saw the result or watched it change.
objectives: Use 가 보니까 and -더라고요 to report firsthand observations.
Use -더니 to connect an observed earlier state to a later change.
Keep -더니 separate from -았/었더니, which is used for your own action leading to a result.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean often marks the source of your information. -더라고요 tells the listener, 'I noticed this myself,' while -더니 tells a small before-and-after story that you watched unfold.

grammarNotes.title: V/A-더라고요 — reporting what I noticed firsthand
grammarNotes.func: Use -더라고요 to report something you personally saw, heard, or felt in the past, usually with a touch of mild surprise or fresh discovery. It means "I noticed / it turned out that..." — the information comes from your own direct experience, not from what someone else told you.

examples.en: That movie was really fun (I saw for myself).
examples.note: You watched it yourself, so you report your own impression with -더라고요.

examples.en: I went outside yesterday, and it was colder than I thought.
examples.note: -더라고요 carries the 'I felt it firsthand' nuance — perfect for weather you experienced.

examples.en: Minsu speaks Korean really well (I noticed).
examples.note: You observed his ability directly, so the slight surprise is built in.

examples.ko: 그 식당에 가 봤는데 사람이 정말 많더라고요.
examples.romanization: geu sikdange ga bwanneunde sarami jeongmal mandeoragoyo.
examples.en: I tried that restaurant, and there were a lot of people.
examples.note: Reporting a scene you saw with your own eyes — a classic -더라고요 use.

keyPoint.label: -더라고요 vs. plain -았/었어요
keyPoint.body: Both talk about the past, but -았/었어요 just states a fact, while -더라고요 frames it as something YOU personally witnessed and are now reporting, often with mild surprise. '비가 왔어요' = it rained (fact); '비가 오더라고요' = I saw that it was raining.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In casual speech -더라고요 is often written informally as -더라구요, but -더라고요 is the standard spelling. In 많더라고요, ㄶ combines with the following ㄷ and makes an aspirated ㅌ sound: [만터라고요].

drill.instruction: Report something you personally noticed, using -더라고요.
drill.model: 그 카페 / 조용하다 → 그 카페가 조용하더라고요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 제가 어제 피곤했어요. / (친구를 보고) 친구가 피곤해 보이더라고요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: -더라고요 usually reports what you observe about OTHER people or the outside world, not your own feeling as you have it. For your own past feelings, use plain -았/었어요. (Your own feelings take -더라고요 only when you look back and 'notice' them as a discovery.)

grammarNotes.title: V/A-더니 — I saw X happen, and then Y followed
grammarNotes.func: Use -더니 to link two things you personally watched: 'I noticed X (in the past), and then Y happened.' The second part is often a change, a result, or a contrast that grows out of the first. The subject of the first part is usually someone else, not you.

formTable.when: After a completed first action (-았/었-), often I-subject

examples.ko: 동생이 아까 울더니 지금은 잘 놀아요.
examples.romanization: dongsaengi akka uldeoni jigeumeun jal norayo.
examples.en: My little brother was crying earlier, and now he's playing happily.
examples.note: You watched the change yourself; -더니 links 'was crying' to the new state 'now playing.'

examples.ko: 아침에는 비가 오더니 오후에는 날씨가 좋아요.
examples.romanization: achimeneun biga odeoni ohueneun nalssiga joayo.
examples.en: It was raining in the morning, but in the afternoon the weather is nice.
examples.note: Here -더니 marks a contrast between two states you saw one after the other.

examples.ko: 친구가 밥을 너무 많이 먹더니 배가 아프대요.
examples.romanization: chinguga babeul neomu mani meokdeoni baega apeudaeyo.
examples.en: My friend ate way too much, and now says his stomach hurts.
examples.note: The watched first part causes the second — a natural cause and effect with -더니.

examples.ko: 동생이 열심히 공부하더니 시험을 잘 봤어요.
examples.romanization: dongsaengi yeolsimhi gongbuhadeoni siheomeul jal bwasseoyo.
examples.en: My brother studied hard, and so he did well on the test.
examples.note: -더니 shows the result naturally following the effort you witnessed.

keyPoint.label: -더니 vs. -았/었더니
keyPoint.body: Plain -더니 reports what you watched someone else (or the world) do, then a follow-up. -았/었더니 usually has 'I' as the subject who finished an action, leading to a result you then found: '제가 밥을 먹었더니 졸려요' (I ate, and now I'm sleepy). Rule of thumb: 더니 → 'they...', 았/었더니 → 'I did..., and then...'.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: In -더니 the 더 is said clearly as [더], with no blending into the next part. With past -었더니, 었더 sounds like [얻떠] with a light tense ㄷ.

drill.instruction: Link a first event you watched to its result, using -더니.
drill.model: 비가 오다 / 길이 막히다 → 비가 오더니 길이 막혀요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.right: 제가 친구를 만났더니 기분이 좋았어요. / 친구가 저를 만나더니 반가워했어요.
englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: When 'I' am the one who finished the first action, use -았/었더니, not plain -더니. Plain -더니 is for watching someone else (or the world), so its first subject is usually NOT 'I.'

exampleSentence.en: When I tried going, it was better than I expected.
exampleSentence.note: Experience leads into a firsthand observation.

exampleSentence.en: There were more people than I expected, I noticed.
exampleSentence.note: Reports what the speaker personally saw.

extendedVocabulary.english: I observed X, and then Y happened

exampleSentence.en: It was quiet at first, and then it quickly got crowded, I noticed.
The food came out faster than expected, I noticed.
It was quiet at first, and then there were quickly more people.
exampleSentence.note: Sets the first stage before a change.

exampleSentence.en: I heard there used to be fewer people.
These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.
When it became lunchtime, the restaurant got crowded, I noticed.
At first, the restaurant was quiet, I noticed.
It was quiet at first, and then there were quickly more people.
These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.
These days, the number of people has increased a lot, I noticed.
These days, the waiting time has decreased, I noticed.
exampleSentence.note: Opposite of 늘다 for observed change.

extendedVocabulary.english: to come to know; to find out

exampleSentence.ko: 직접 가 보니까 왜 유명한지 알게 됐어요.
exampleSentence.en: After going there myself, I found out why it is famous.

exampleSentence.ko: 일주일 동안 분위기가 어떻게 변하는지 관찰했어요.
exampleSentence.en: I observed how the atmosphere changed over a week.

extendedDialogue.setting: A friend asks about a new restaurant after someone visited it.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.ko: 어제 새 식당에 가 보니까 어땠어요?
lines.romanization: eoje sae sikdange ga bonikka eottaesseoyo?
lines.en: How was it when you tried going to the new restaurant yesterday?
lines.grammarNote: 가 보니까 asks for a report based on actual experience.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: It was quiet at first, and then it quickly got crowded, I noticed.
lines.grammarNote: -더니 connects the observed first state to the later change.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: It came out faster than expected, and the taste was good too.
lines.grammarNote: 생각보다 plus -더라고요 compares expectation with firsthand experience.

lines.speaker: 민서
lines.en: I heard there used to be fewer people.
lines.grammarNote: 예전에는 sets up the past state.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Right. These days, the atmosphere has changed a lot, I noticed.
lines.grammarNote: 요즘은 and -더라고요 report the current state the speaker noticed.

readingText.title: 가 보니까 생각보다 괜찮더라고요
readingText.body: 새 식당이나 카페에 다녀온 뒤에는 그냥 '좋았어요'라고 말할 수도 있지만, 직접 보고 느낀 느낌을 살리려면 '-더라고요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '가 보니까 생각보다 조용하더라고요'라고 하면 내가 직접 가서 알게 된 정보라는 느낌이 들어요. 시간이 지나면서 변한 모습을 말할 때는 '-더니'가 좋아요. 예를 들어 '처음에는 조용하더니 금방 붐비더라고요'라고 하면 처음 상태와 나중 상태가 한 장면처럼 이어져요. 하지만 내 행동 때문에 생긴 결과라면 '많이 먹었더니 졸렸어요'처럼 '-았/었더니'를 써야 해요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: After visiting a restaurant or cafe, -더라고요 lets you report what you personally noticed. -더니 links an observed first state to a later change. For the result of your own action, use -았/었더니 instead.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 직접 보고 느낀 내용을 말할 때 어떤 표현이 자연스러워요?
처음 상태와 나중 상태를 이어 말할 때 어떤 표현이 좋아요?
내 행동 때문에 생긴 결과에는 어떤 형태를 써야 해요?

culturalNote.title: Korean marks how you know
culturalNote.body: A Korean review often hints at the evidence source. -더라고요 tells the listener this came from your own experience, not just a rumor or general fact.
culturalNote.tip: Before using -더라고요, ask: did I personally see, hear, feel, try, or realize this?

inlineExercises.prompt: You visited the restaurant yourself and noticed it was crowded. Which sentence fits best?
Which sentence shows an observed change over time?
inlineExercises.explanation: -더니 connects the observed first state with the later change.

inlineExercises.prompt: You ate a lot, so you became sleepy. Which form is correct?
inlineExercises.explanation: Use -았/었더니 for your own action leading to a result.

inlineExercises.prompt: 그 식당___ 가 보니까 생각보다 조용하더라고요. (When I tried going to that restaurant...)
inlineExercises.explanation: 가 보다 is movement/trying a place, so the destination takes 에. 에서 would mark an action happening at the place.
-더라고요 reports what you personally noticed. 붐비다 becomes 붐비더라고요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'When I tried going there, it was quieter than expected.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 가 보니까 sets up what you learned by trying it yourself. -더라고요 reports the firsthand observation.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'At first it was quiet, and then it quickly got crowded.'
inlineExercises.explanation: -더니 connects an observed earlier state to a later change. 금방 makes the change feel quick.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence about your own action result: '제가 많이 먹더니 졸렸어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: For your own action leading to a result, use -았/었더니. Plain -더니 is better for something you observed in others or outside yourself.

inlineExercises.prompt: You saw a shop get crowded over time. Which sentence fits?
inlineExercises.explanation: -더니 fits the observed change from quiet to crowded. The other choices either misuse the subject or switch to a different grammar.

inlineExercises.prompt: Say: 'These days it turned out to be crowded.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 요즘은 sets the current period. -더라고요 makes it sound like something you noticed yourself.

bullets: -더라고요 reports what you personally noticed or realized.
-더니 connects an observed earlier state/action with a later change.
가 보니까, 생각보다, 처음에는, 예전에는, and 요즘은 make the observation scene clearer.
Use -았/었더니, not plain -더니, for your own action causing a result.

writingTask.prompt: Tell a friend about a cafe you went to recently: report what you noticed when you got there, and how it had changed from before.
writingTask.hint: Report what you saw firsthand with -더라고요 (조용하더라고요), and link 'I noticed X, and then Y' with -더니 (사람이 늘더니 붐비더라고요). Use 예전에는 / 요즘은 for the before-and-after.
writingTask.model: 어제 그 카페에 가 봤는데, 생각보다 사람이 많더라고요. 예전에는 조용했는데 요즘은 손님이 늘더니 정말 붐비더라고요. 그래도 커피는 맛있더라고요.
writingTask.modelEn: I went to that cafe yesterday, and there were more people than I expected. It used to be quiet, but these days the customers increased and then it got really crowded. Still, the coffee was good (I found).

canDo: Report something I personally saw or felt, with mild surprise, using -더라고요 (붐비더라고요)
Link 'I noticed X, and then Y followed' with -더니 (늘더니 붐비더라고요)
Contrast before and after with 예전에는 / 요즘은
Describe a place changing over time (조용하다 → 붐비다, 달라지다)
